disclosures.name: TestCountMallocs
disclosures.reason: An AllocsPerRun family over 24 Sprintf/Fprintf/Errorf legs. Since Go 1.26 each leg must EQUAL Go's own mallocTest count (0 to 4); Go 1.24 asserted at most that count, and its message read `want <=`. 20 of the 24 legs differ in the converted run. Sprintf("") and Sprintf("xxx") match, and two noliteral legs (Fprintf(buf, "%x") and Fprintf(buf, "%v")) match only because one extra charge offsets one uncounted interface box. DEFERRED, not alloc-count-semantics: the run's unit note reads `counted ... go2cs-runtime object allocations ... an allocation COUNT per run` -- Go's own unit. ONE mechanism is named and read, and it is paid by every Sprintf/Fprintf leg with arguments: the variadic pack. The call site is C# 13 `params Span<any>` (the compiler's stack pack, like Go's non-escaping ...any backing array), and Sprintf/Fprintf's first act, `aʗp.slice()`, copies it to the heap (golib slice.cs `slice<T>(this Span<T>)` -> AllocationCounter.CopyOf) -- one charged array per call where Go allocates none. On 8 legs it is the whole difference: each reads Go's count plus one. The REST is NOT yet attributed: 6 Sprintf/Fprintf legs carry 1 or 2 more than the pack, Fprintf(buf, "%x %x %x") over three pointer arguments carries 12 more, and the 4 Errorf legs differ by 2 to 7 (Errorf copies its arguments through `sslice()`, not the charged `slice()`). One leg reads BELOW Go, Fprintf(buf, "%v") of a []int at 3 against 4; the equality assertion now reports it, and the counter's coverage allows it, because C# boxing is not counted. So this entry is deferred on a partially named mechanism and says so.
disclosures.want: Go's exact mallocTest count per leg, 0 to 4 allocations per run (19 of the 24 legs want 0 or 1)
disclosures.reading: 20 of 24 legs differ, per run, got/want, at 7289accf43 on linux (Release, tiering off, .NET 10.0.12, go1.26.9): Sprintf("%x") 1/0 and 2/1, Sprintf("%80000s") 5/3, Sprintf("%s") 3/1, Sprintf("%x %x") 2/1, Sprintf("%g") 4/1, Fprintf(buf,"%s") 2/0, 2/0 and 2/1, Fprintf(buf,"%x") 1/0, 1/0 and 1/0, Fprintf(buf,"%v") 3/4 and 1/0, Fprintf(buf,"%80000s") 4/2, Fprintf(buf,"%x %x %x") 13/0, Errorf("hello") 3/0, Errorf("hello: %x") 9/2, sink = Errorf("hello") 3/1, sink = Errorf("hello: %x") 9/2. Matching: Sprintf("") 0/0, Sprintf("xxx") 1/1, Fprintf(buf,"%x") noliteral 1/1, Fprintf(buf,"%v") noliteral 1/1. A LOWER BOUND by the host's own note. At Go 1.24.13 the table had 16 legs and 15 read over their bound.
disclosures.plan: first the named site: a non-copying slice view over a params span the callee does not retain (Sprintf/Fprintf hand `a` to doPrintf and drop it when the printer is freed), which removes one charged array per call on every Sprintf/Fprintf leg with arguments; then attribute the remainder leg by leg from the emission, starting with Fprintf(buf, "%x %x %x") (12 beyond the pack) and Errorf("hello") (no arguments, 3 against 0). The entry retires when a run reads every leg equal to Go's count with the counter still charging the path.
